{{Short description|Unique ring consisting of one element}}
{{other uses|Ring 0 (disambiguation){{!}}Ring 0}}
{{Ring theory sidebar}}
In [[ring theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''zero ring'''{{sfn|Artin|1991|p=347|ps=}}{{sfnm|1a1=Atiyah|1a2=Macdonald|1y=1969|1p=1|2a1=Bosch|2y=2012|2p=10|3a1=Bourbaki|3p=101|4a1=Lam|4y=2003|4p=1}} or '''trivial ring''' is the unique [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] (up to [[isomorphism]]) consisting of one element. (Less commonly, the term "zero ring" is used to refer to any <!-- "rng" here is not a typo; see the rng page, and the Manual of Style.-->[[Rng (algebra)#Rng of square zero|rng of square zero]], i.e., a [[Rng (algebra)|rng]] in which {{math|{{nowrap|1=''xy'' = 0}}}} for all {{mvar|x}} and {{mvar|y}}. This article refers to the one-element ring.)

In the [[category of rings]], the zero ring is the [[terminal object]], whereas the ring of integers '''Z''' is the [[initial object]].

== Definition ==
The zero ring, denoted {0} or simply '''0''', consists of the [[singleton (mathematics)|one-element set]] {0} with the [[Binary operation|operations]] + and · defined such that 0 + 0 = 0 and 0 · 0 = 0.

== Properties ==
* The zero ring is the unique ring in which the [[additive identity]] 0 and [[multiplicative identity]] 1 coincide.{{sfn|Artin|1991|p=347|ps=}}{{sfn|Lang|2002|p=83|ps=}}  (Proof: If {{nowrap|1=1 = 0}} in a ring ''R'', then for all ''r'' in ''R'', we have {{nowrap|1=''r'' = 1''r'' = 0''r'' = 0}}. The proof of the last equality is found [[v:Proofs of elementary ring properties|here]].)
* The zero ring is commutative.
* The element 0 in the zero ring is a [[unit (ring theory)|unit]], serving as its own [[multiplicative inverse]].
* The [[unit group]] of the zero ring is the [[trivial group]] {0}.
* The element 0 in the zero ring is not a [[zero divisor#Zero as a zero divisor|zero divisor]].
* The only [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] in the zero ring is the zero ideal {0}, which is also the unit ideal, equal to the whole ring.  This ideal is neither [[maximal ideal|maximal]] nor [[prime ideal|prime]].
* The zero ring is generally excluded from [[field (mathematics)|field]]s, while occasionally called as the ''trivial field''. Excluding it agrees with the fact that its zero ideal is not maximal. (When mathematicians speak of the "[[field with one element]]", they are referring to a non-existent object, and their intention is to define the category that would be the category of schemes over this object if it existed.)
* The zero ring is generally excluded from [[integral domain]]s.{{sfn|Lam|2003|p=3|ps=}}  Whether the zero ring is considered to be a [[domain (ring theory)|domain]] at all is a matter of convention, but there are two advantages to considering it not to be a domain.  First, this agrees with the definition that a domain is a ring in which 0 is the only zero divisor (in particular, 0 is required to be a zero divisor, which fails in the zero ring).  Second, this way, for a positive integer ''n'', the ring '''Z'''/''n'''''Z''' is a domain if and only if ''n'' is prime, but 1 is not prime.
* For each ring ''A'', there is a unique [[ring homomorphism]] from ''A'' to the zero ring.  Thus the zero ring is a [[terminal object]] in the [[category of rings]].{{sfn|Hartshorne|1977|p=80|ps=}}
* If ''A'' is a nonzero ring, then there is no ring homomorphism from the zero ring to ''A''.  In particular, the zero ring is not a [[subring]] of any nonzero ring.{{sfn|Hartshorne|1977|p=80|ps=}}
* The zero ring is the unique ring of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] 1.
* The only [[module (mathematics)|module]] for the zero ring is the zero module.  It is free of rank א for any [[cardinal number]] א.
* The zero ring is not a [[local ring]].  It is, however, a [[semilocal ring]].
* The zero ring is [[Artinian ring|Artinian]] and (therefore) [[Noetherian ring|Noetherian]].
* The [[spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] of the zero ring is the empty [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]].{{sfn|Hartshorne|1977|p=80|ps=}}
* The [[Krull dimension]] of the zero ring is &minus;∞.
* The zero ring is [[semisimple ring|semisimple]] but not [[simple ring|simple]].
* The zero ring is not a [[central simple algebra]] over any field.
* The [[total quotient ring]] of the zero ring is itself.

== Constructions ==
* For any ring ''A'' and ideal ''I'' of ''A'', the [[quotient ring|quotient]] ''A''/''I'' is the zero ring if and only if {{nowrap|1=''I'' = ''A''}}, i.e. if and only if ''I'' is the [[unit ideal]].
* For any commutative ring ''A'' and [[multiplicative set]] ''S'' in ''A'', the [[localization of a ring|localization]] ''S''<sup>−1</sup>''A'' is the zero ring if and only if ''S'' contains 0.
* If ''A'' is any ring, then the ring M<sub>0</sub>(''A'') of 0 × 0 [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]] over ''A'' is the zero ring.
* The [[direct product]] of an empty collection of rings is the zero ring.
* The [[endomorphism ring]] of the [[trivial group]] is the zero ring.
* The ring of [[continuous function|continuous]] real-valued functions on the empty [[topological space]] is the zero ring.
